findings.claim: The origin-changed row was reduced to a pointer and the operator steps moved into a new subsection. Step 2 (tombstone old chunk keys) depends on the old Source-Id, which the table row no longer mentions. The procedure is also ordered with `supersedes` first and the sync last. Nothing says that step 4 (propagation to the old page) happens only after the tombstone promotes. A reader of the table alone now sees 'retiring it is the operator procedure below' with no mention that old chunks must be retired as well. This is a recall risk for agents that read only the table. The section also cites a repo-internal Go source path (`longterm-mem/internal/promote/propagate_cards.go`) in a contract mirrored to every runtime, which is the same kind of external reference the commit removed for memorycard.

The manifest last-element rule now says the last element is the `**Chunk-Status**` inventory when it has entries, otherwise `**Chunks-Saved**`. The commit's own log states `Render` writes `**Chunks-Saved**` for every manifest and the inventory only conditionally, but the rule gives no ordering guarantee between them in the text, so a reader cannot tell where `**Chunks-Saved**` sits relative to the other fields when the inventory is empty. The sentence 'nothing precedes it' is also unchanged and can be read as contradicting the 'last element' wording for a single-field block.

The hard no-op bullet now defers to 'the contract's chunk `**Status**` rule' for single-chunk records at the manifest key, instead of stating the `complete` live value inline. The skill reader must now chase a cross-reference to learn what value to expect, which weakens the skill's self-containedness for a rule that gates a no-op decision.

evidence: Diff shows the origin-changed table row reduced to one sentence, with the old-chunk tombstone, supersedes and propagation steps moved into a numbered subsection (contract lines 150-170).
Diff shows the manifest last-element sentence rewrapped and extended with the 'otherwise Chunks-Saved' alternative (contract lines 62-64).
Diff shows the SKILL.md hard no-op bullet replacing an inline explanation with a reference to the contract's chunk Status rule.
